bc_snowbound.blurb: Snowbound is a single granite wall beside Highway 16 in northern British Columbia, part of the Terrace climbing zone, with the trailhead about 65 km west of town. There are five sport routes, running from the 5.10 range up into 5.12, so it suits climbers already comfortable on harder terrain rather than beginners. The stone is coarse and solid, vertical to slightly overhanging, with small edges and the occasional pocket. Every line finishes at anchors, and a handline connects the tops of three of them. The face stays dry in light rain unless a strong wind drives it in. A lookout just past the wall gives a view over the Skeena River valley.

bc_hard_rock.blurb: Hard Rock is a big boulder in the Rogue's Gallery bouldering zone of Cheakamus Canyon, along the Sea to Sky corridor. It is the largest block you can see from the trail, sitting just beyond Classic Rock. Five problems start at V1 and top out at V4, with two at V2 and one at V3, so there is something for climbers across the lower and middle grades. Boulders in this zone are mostly covered with lichen, and the top-outs can carry some moss, so check the finish before committing. The block has room for further problems.

bc_hoax_boulder.blurb: Hoax Boulder is a tall, cube-shaped block in the Left Fork section of the Sasquatch Boulders, part of the Elbow Lake bouldering in the Fraser Valley. It has five problems: two at V1, two at V2 and one at V3, so it works for climbers in the lower to middle grades. Starts are mostly sit-starts using slopers and side pulls, followed by edges. The rock is a bit frail in places. The block sits only a few steps uphill from the Quick and Nimble boulder, and the way off is a down-climb, so pads and a spotter are worth bringing.
